### Observed differences

- In the later window, A06 appears in about 12% of traces (down from 27%), its mean occurrences per trace dropped from 0.29 to 0.15, and its position shifted later (mean relative position from 0.25 to 0.44). [OCC002, POS001]
- A02 appears in about 12% of traces (up from 4.5%), though the number of traces containing it is small (23 vs 9). [OCC001]
- The core activities A26 and A27 moved earlier (mean position from 0.62 to 0.53 and 0.47 to 0.38 respectively), while A35, A36, and A41 moved later (from about 0.41–0.42 to 0.58–0.59). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- The order between A26 and A35/A36/A41 reversed: before, A35/A36/A41 preceded A26 in about 99% of traces; after, A26 precedes them in about 97–98%. The same reversal holds for A27 with A35/A36/A41. [REL001–REL006]
- Successor changes: A25 now goes to A27 in about 98% of its outgoing transitions (before it went to A35, A36, A41 in about 39%, 32%, 27%). A26 now goes to A35/A36/A41 (about 34%/32%/30%) instead of A30 (about 99% before). A35/A36/A41 now go to A30 (about 35%/30%/32%) instead of A27 (about 28–37% before). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]
- LAG: A25 and A27 are now adjacent (lag 1 in 98.5% vs lag 4 in 93.5% before). A26 and A30 are now far apart (lag 4 in 91% vs lag 1 in 99% before). A16 and A27 are now far apart (lag 5 in 99% vs lag 1 in 100% before). [LAG005, LAG009, LAG003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a reordering of the process: A26 and A27 now occur before A35, A36, and A41, whereas before they occurred after them; A30 now occurs after A35/A36/A41 instead of directly after A26. This is directly shown by the reversed relative orders (REL), the shifted positions (POS), the changed successor distributions (DIR), and the changed lags (LAG). The number of qualifying items (33) far exceeds the 0.76 expected by chance, so the overall pattern is not a sampling artefact. A separate change is that A06 became less frequent and moved later, but this is not part of the main reordering hypothesis.

Other differences: A06 participation decreased and its successors became more varied; A02 participation increased, though with limited support.

A competing explanation that cannot be fully ruled out is that the observed reordering reflects a change in the mix of variants rather than a single uniform process change, but the consistency across multiple indicators makes this unlikely.
